_comment: Syncline config — one per repo you want to mirror to a GitHub Project (v2). Copy this to e.g. configs/<yourproject>.config.json and fill it in. This file is the AUTHORITATIVE schema: it documents EVERY field the adapter (syncline_build_manifest.py) and the engine (syncline_import.py, syncline_sync.py) read. Each real field is preceded by a `_<field>` comment key (standard JSON has no comments). Nothing about your repo/owner/project is hard-coded in the scripts — all of it is config-driven and lives here.
_paths_note: All *_file paths below resolve RELATIVE TO THIS CONFIG FILE's own directory; pass an absolute path to override. State/manifest/cache files are engine-owned bookkeeping — keep them out of version control (they are local-only and do not travel to teammates/CI).
_project_name: The GitHub Project (v2) board title to mirror onto, matched case-insensitively. Required. No default.
_repo_owner: The owner (user or org login) of both the repo and the project. Required. No default.
_owner_type: Whether repo_owner is an 'org' or a 'user' — selects the GraphQL root used to resolve the project. Matched exactly: only the literal 'org' selects the organization root; any other value (including 'organization' or 'User') falls through to the user root. Default: 'org'.
_repo_name: The repository that issues are created in. Required. No default.
_status_map: Maps each RAW plan status (left) to the exact board Status option NAME (right). The board must already have these options (matched case-insensitively). Add a row for every status your plan uses: the adapter fails validation on a plan status missing here, while the sync silently skips an unmapped status rather than erroring. Required. No default.
_done_statuses: Which RAW statuses are terminal: an item with one of these is CLOSED on the board (a non-terminal status reopens it). Default: ["done"].
_type_field_name: Custom single-select field tagging each item by its Work Type (Epic/Story). NOTE: 'Type' is a RESERVED Projects v2 field name and cannot be created — use 'Work Type'. The importer creates this field if absent (except under --dry-run); the sync never creates it and only sets it when the field already exists. Default: 'Work Type'.
_files: Where the plan and Syncline's own bookkeeping live. For a BMAD layout these sit under _bmad-output (gitignored). plan_file is the sprint status the sync reads for per-item status; epics_file (+ optional story_spec_glob) feed the manifest builder with titles; manifest_file/state_file/cache_file are Syncline's own artifacts.
_plan_file: The plan the sync reads for per-item status (a BMAD sprint-status.yaml). Resolved relative to this config's dir. Read by the adapter and the sync.
_epics_file: The plan source the adapter reads epic/story TITLES from (a BMAD epics.md). Resolved relative to this config's dir. Read by the adapter only.
_story_spec_glob: OPTIONAL glob of story spec files whose frontmatter `title:` gives nicer story titles than the slug. Omit to fall back to a readable title derived from the story key. Read by the adapter only.
_manifest_file: The manifest the adapter WRITES and the engine READS — Syncline's one on-disk contract. Required by the importer (it exits if the manifest is unreadable); optional for the sync (used only to title brand-new items it creates). Resolved relative to this config's dir.
_state_file: Engine-owned import bookkeeping (per-item issue/project ids) that makes import idempotent + resumable. Local-only; do not commit.
_cache_file: Engine-owned sync cache (plan sha256 + resolved board ids + last-seen statuses) that makes an unchanged plan a no-op. Local-only; do not commit.
_label: Short tag printed in the sync's one-line 'project synced' message so you can tell which board changed. Default: project_name.
label: subby
_regexes: ADVANCED. Line patterns for parsing the plan; override only if your plan format differs from a BMAD sprint-status.yaml. Two independent sets with DIFFERENT capture groups: (1) the SYNC reads epic_line_regex/story_line_regex where group(1)=key, group(2)=status; story_key_regex and epic_num_from_story_regex classify a key and extract its epic number. (2) the ADAPTER reads manifest_epic_regex (groups: 1=key, 2=epicNum, 3=status) and manifest_story_regex (groups: 1=key, 2=epicNum, 3=storyNum, 4=status) — it needs the NUMBERS, so these are kept separate from the sync patterns. Each has a built-in default; set a key here only to override it.
